title: The Day the Kettle Refused
skyStory: The waxing crescent, eleven percent lit, is still bouncing around Aries like a kid on a trampoline. It has decided today is for pranks. Not mean ones. Just small mischief: a kettle that takes forever, a sock that vanishes, a word you cannot remember. Mars thinks this is hilarious. Saturn is writing a strongly worded letter to the management.

reading: Something in the kitchen will refuse to cooperate this morning. The kettle, the toaster, the drawer that sticks. The moon is testing your sense of humour. Pass the test by laughing out loud, even if you are alone. Especially if you are alone.

Midday brings a funny coincidence of words: you will think of a word just before someone says it. Write it down. It is your word of the day. Use it three times in conversation before dinner, as naturally as possible. If anyone notices, tell them the Aries moon made you do it. They will nod, because nobody argues with the moon, and the cabin will chuckle quietly to itself.
joel.mission: Pick an unusual word like flummox and slip it into three separate conversations before dinner without anyone catching on.
joel.omen: A sock without its partner sock in the laundry. It means a small mystery is about to solve itself cheerfully.

reading: The Wood Rat smells mischief on the breeze and decides to join in rather than fight it. Today you get to be the gentle trickster: hide a small, kind surprise for someone to find later. A note in a coat pocket. A drawing on a fogged mirror.

Around 2:45 pm, a coworker or a neighbour will say something so oddly specific that you will wonder if they have been reading your diary. They have not. The moon simply tapped them on the shoulder and whispered your thought into their ear as a joke. Laugh. Tell them, they are correct. Leave it at that, mysterious and smiling, like a rat in a wizard hat.
nancy.mission: Leave a small hidden note of kindness somewhere for someone to find later, then walk away whistling like nothing happened.
nancy.omen: Writing appearing on a foggy window or mirror. It means someone is thinking about you warmly right now.

together.text: Send each other the most dramatic possible description of one small inconvenience from today, written like an epic poem. The kettle took four minutes becomes a saga. The winner is whoever makes the other one snort first.

game.intro: The kettle refused to boil, so the crew refuses to be right. Wrong answers only, please.
game.question: At what temperature in Celsius does water boil at sea level?
